newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries open higher, stronger dollar helps.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries open higher, stronger dollar helps.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices opened higher ahead of the U.S. retail sales report on Thursday, aided by a stronger dollar.

The dollar rebounded against the mark and yen after the director general of the International Finance Bureau of Japan's Ministry of Finance, Eisuke Sakakibara, said that trade issues were being "played up excessively" and that Japan's current account surplus would not be a major topic for the Group of Seven major industrial nations meeting in Denver later in June.
In opening trade, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was up 6/32 to 97-14/32, yielding 6.83 percent.
While the stronger dollar was supportive for Treasury prices, the Treasury market's main focus is on economic data due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT.
The Commerce Department's May retail sales report is expected to be the most important piece of economic data released on Thursday.
Economists polled by Reuters forecast a 0.4 percent rise in retail sales in May versus a 0.3-percent drop in April.
Without auto sales, retail sales are expected to be up a modest 0.3 percent for May after a 0.1 percent slip in April.

The retail sales are of key interest to the market because Federal Reserve monetary policy makers are focused on the strength of consumer demand. Consumer spending is responsible for two-thirds of GDP (Gross Domestic Product). If consumer demand looked as if it were slowing, policymakers could expect that production eventually would slow to stay in sync with demand, analysts said.

Also, at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, the Labor Department will release first-time claims for jobless benefits for the week ended June 7. Economists polled by Reuters forecast a total of 326,000 new filings for the week after a surge to 337,000 new claims in the week that included the Memorial Day holiday.
At 0900 EDT/1300 GMT, the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta will release its Southeast Manufacturing Survey for the month of May.
Analysts said the retail sales report was likely to determine the market's direction for the day.
Another market friendly report, the May Producer Price Index (PPI), is due on Friday, they noted.
At 0800 EDT/1200 GMT, three-month bill rates were up one basis point to 4.85 percent. Six-month bill rates were unchanged at 5.20 percent. Year bill rates were down two basis points to 5.43 percent.

Two-year notes were up 1/32 to 100-5/32, yielding 6.16 percent. Five-year notes were priced at 100-7/32 to yield 6.45 percent. Ten-year notes were trading at 100-15/32, up 3/32, to yield 6.56 percent.
